articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. The 2026 midterm elections have been the most expensive in history, with more than $11 billion being spent on political ads. While Democratic candidates have outraised Republicans in individual donations by appealing directly to voters, Republicans have received the lion’s share of money from super PACs (political action committees) funded by a small number of the wealthiest elites in the United States. The single biggest election-cycle donor is, unsurprisingly, the richest human on the planet. articles.title: Portland’s Socialists Have Built a Political Machine
articles.author: Roman Broszkowski
articles.content_excerpt: Over the last two years, the Portland, Oregon, chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) has developed a reputation for punching far above its city’s weight. The chapter sits just behind the New York, Los Angeles, and Washington, DC, chapters in terms of size, and roughly one in two hundred Portlanders is a member (compared to about one in 530 New Yorkers). Today one-third of Portland’s city council actively participates in the group’s Socialists in Office Committee (SIOC); this election cycle, the chapter ran candidates for state and county office. articles.title: Xi Jinping’s Chinese Dream Has Replaced the Maoist Credo
articles.author: Teemu Ruskola
articles.content_excerpt: Since 1978, China has undergone a series of seismic changes in its economic order that have radically altered its citizens’ relationship to both labor and land. They have unmade the socialist working class and are in the process of expropriating the peasantry, transforming both into a propertyless proletariat. At the same time, China’s political structure has not undergone a similar revolution. Accordingly, the contradiction between its systems of economic and political organization is increasingly acute. A Single Story The disjunctive fates of rural and urban China have been part of a single story ever since the establishment of the People’s Republic. articles.title: The Bases of US Empire Are Crumbling
articles.author: Costas Lapavitsas
articles.content_excerpt: Imperialism is again at the forefront of world politics. Large-scale war has become a permanent feature of the present era, from Ukraine to Gaza. Donald Trump’s second term has added a tariff war, threats to annex Greenland, the abduction of Venezuela’s president, and, together with Israel, an unprovoked war on Iran. This is not the whim of one man, for the confrontation with China began under Trump’s first term and deepened under Joe Biden. At the same time, politics across the mature capitalist countries is in deep turmoil. In the United States, the Left has become a force in mass politics, with a democratic socialist as mayor of New York and widespread opposition to Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Israel’s genocide in Palestine, and the war on Iran. articles.title: The Volkswagen Crisis Exposes Germany’s Industrial Decline
articles.author: Alexander Görlach
articles.content_excerpt: On October 9, European Union Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič announced an agreement on hybrid vehicles, following two days of talks with Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao in Beijing. According to Šefčovič, over the next four years or so, Chinese exports of full and plug-in hybrids to the EU are expected to fall below half of previous forecasts. The specific quotas, minimum prices, or monitoring mechanisms were not disclosed. The agreement is provisional, with further talks scheduled for 2027. Shortly before Šefčovič’s trip, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and French President Emmanuel Macron had been putting pressure on the European Commission. articles.title: Fighting ICE From the Ground Up
articles.author: Guest Author
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. When immigration agents take a father from his workplace, the consequences extend far beyond the moment of arrest. His children may lose their primary caregiver. His family may suddenly face eviction or hunger. Relatives may spend days trying to determine where he has been taken, while struggling to raise money for an attorney, telephone calls, or food inside a detention facility. Those were among the experiences described at the October 2026 Left Coast Forum at Cal State LA, where grassroots organizers gathered for a panel titled The Impact of ICE Session I: How Communities Have Responded to ICE Raids and Where We Go From Here. articles.title: The Tasks for DSA After the Blue Wave
articles.author: Bread & Roses Caucus
articles.content_excerpt: On November 3rd, the American people sent a decisive message. We are sick and tired of MAGA and the Trump administration, of the cost of living crisis, of war, of corruption, of corporate greed, of billionaires dominating our political system. Alongside an overwhelming rejection of the far-right, voters also chose to send the largest number of democratic socialists in 100 years into the halls of power. Our movement elected over 100 democratic socialists with a clear message: we need a government and economy that works for working people, not the billionaires, capitalists, warmongers, and genocidaires.
